Title: 615,000 Americans Are Diagnosed With Ménière's - The 3 Triggers to Cut

Description:
If your vertigo comes bundled with ringing ears, hearing changes, or a plugged-up feeling, it's not just ordinary dizziness. Ménière's disease happens when fluid builds up in the inner ear (endolymphatic hydrops), and about 615,000 U.S. adults are diagnosed with it, with up to 100,000 new cases every year.

Unlike BPPV or vestibular neuritis, attacks bring vertigo, tinnitus, hearing loss, and ear fullness together, lasting 20 minutes to several hours. Three habits make attacks worse: sodium, caffeine and alcohol, and stress or poor sleep.

Keep sodium under 1,500-2,000mg a day, swap coffee for decaf, and keep a consistent sleep schedule. If symptoms keep recurring, see an ENT for a proper diagnosis.
